compiled_state.title: Make forbidden-action HARD-GATEs in brainstorm/sprint/fix-bug/implementation-plan load-bearing via tool-use-time enforcement
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Context

Forbidden-action HARD-GATEs in /dso:brainstorm, /dso:sprint, and /dso:fix-bug (e.g., "do not edit code during the dialogue phase", "do not dispatch a new batch over uncommitted work", "do not edit source before a RED test") are reachable when an agent is challenged but are NOT load-bearing during silent execution — nothing stops a violating tool call at tool-use time. This epic makes a curated seed of those gates load-bearing via a phase-aware PreToolUse hook that reads durable per-skill (skill, phase) state, fails open + observably when phase is uncertain, grows the gate set through a brainstorm-confirmed path, and provides a user-only audited override.

EPIC_CLASS: class:architectural

## Success Criteria

SC1: Each gated skill (brainstorm, sprint, fix-bug) writes a durable per-skill phase marker under a session-partitioned path within the artifacts dir (resolved via get_artifacts_dir()), e.g. `phase-state/<session_id>/<skill>`, recording {phase, session_id, timestamp}; the session_id is sourced from the canonical session identifier (the PreToolUse input `.session_id` on the hook side; the session-id file on the skill side). Each skill refreshes the timestamp at each named phase step (heartbeat) and removes the marker at skill exit. The marker freshness TTL is a documented config key with a default. A State Lifecycle Owner Block in this epic names CREATE/UPDATE/CONSUME/RETIRE for every marker. (implementation-plan is intentionally NOT instrumented in this epic — it has no seed gate; it is added via SC4 growth when a gate for it is confirmed.)
Verify-intent: a fixture run of each gated skill writes its marker under the session-partitioned path carrying the current phase + session id; the marker is absent after the skill's exit/cleanup step; two simulated concurrent sessions do not overwrite each other's marker.

SC2: A phase-aware PreToolUse hook reads every phase marker whose session_id matches the active session and whose timestamp is within the freshness TTL, and blocks an in-flight tool call (exit 2) when the call violates a seed-registry gate for any active (skill, phase); otherwise it allows the call (exit 0). When no fresh same-session marker resolves the phase, the hook allows the call and emits an observable warning, distinguishing "phase indeterminate at session start" (single informational warning) from "a marker existed for this skill and then went stale mid-session" (escalated warning naming the skill/phase, so silent enforcement rot is surfaced); warnings are rate-limited/deduped to avoid alarm fatigue. The hook supports a shadow/log-only mode that records would-have-blocked decisions without blocking, for baseline measurement. Block decisions evaluate the union of all active markers' gates.
Verify-intent: synthetic PreToolUse JSON — a gate-violating call with a matching fresh same-session marker is blocked (exit 2); the same call with a missing/stale/other-session marker is allowed (exit 0) with the appropriate (start vs stale) warning; shadow mode logs the decision and returns exit 0.

SC3: The seed registry enforces exactly three gates, each emitting a specific ordered remediation in its block message:
(a) brainstorm Phase 1–2 blocks Edit/Write whose target realpath is inside the repo working tree (temp-space paths allowed), AND blocks a Bash move/copy/patch-apply whose destination realpath lands inside the working tree (closing the temp-then-move evasion); the realpath containment check resolves symlinks (e.g., /tmp -> /private/tmp on macOS) before deciding.
(b) sprint blocks a new Agent/Task batch dispatch while the current session has uncommitted prior-batch results OR un-harvested/un-removed prior-batch agent worktrees (worktrees attributed to other sessions via WORKTREE_TRACKING are ignored); the block message names which condition tripped and the exact resolving command.
(c) fix-bug blocks Edit/Write to a non-test source file unless a current-session RED signal exists for that source — a failing test mapped to it via the test-gate `test-gate-status` failed_tests record and the `.test-index` source→test mapping, established by fix-bug RUNNING the RED test at Phase E Step 1 BEFORE source edits — OR fix-bug has recorded a positive "behavioral / no-executable-RED" classification for the bug. Absence of a failing test alone is NOT an exemption (that would invert TDD into edit-freely-if-no-test); the gate blocks when neither a RED signal nor a recorded behavioral classification is present. Test-file edits are always allowed.
Verify-intent: a fixture exercises each gate — the violation is blocked, the happy-path call is allowed; for (a) a temp-then-move into the repo is blocked; for (c) the RED-confirmed source edit is allowed, the recorded-behavioral-bug edit is allowed, and an edit with neither signal is blocked.

SC4: When an epic under /dso:brainstorm modifies one of the gated SKILL.md files and introduces a new forbidden-action gate, brainstorm surfaces the candidate (skill, phase, forbidden-tool-or-action) using a neutral fixed template (skill, phase, forbidden action, the SKILL.md line that introduced it) with no agent-authored recommendation to decline, and on user confirmation appends it to the seed registry; declined candidates are persistently logged so a pattern of declines is auditable. (Growth candidates are surfaced only during /dso:brainstorm; gates introduced by sprint/fix-bug skill edits outside a brainstorm are out of scope for auto-surfacing — see Out of Scope.)
Verify-intent: a fixture brainstorm over an epic that adds a forbidden-action line to a gated SKILL.md surfaces the candidate via the neutral template; on confirm the registry gains the entry; on decline the registry is unchanged and a decline record is written.

SC5: A user-invoked `dso forbidden-action-override --reason="..."` grants a single override consumed by the next block (a subsequent forbidden call is blocked again); the grant requires an explicit current-turn user instruction authorizing the override (interactive/TTY presence alone is insufficient — an agent rationalizing "on the user's behalf" must not satisfy it), and the audit record captures the user-approval evidence alongside reason, timestamp, and attribution (reusing the commit-override audit-trail pattern). The token is session-scoped (a token whose session_id differs is never consumed). Under DSO_FBKY_AUTONOMOUS_MODE the override is not self-granted to the agent.
Verify-intent: a fixture shows one-shot consumption (next block re-applies), an audit record written with reason+timestamp+approval-evidence, an agent-context (no current-turn user instruction) invocation rejected, a token from another session not consumed, and the autonomous-mode path not self-granted.

## Closure Checks

- Self-use dogfood: at af26's own sprint Phase I, the hook + seed registry are deployed and active; a representative happy-path session trace of each of the three gated skills (including an adversarial temp-then-move probe) runs with the hook active and produces zero spurious blocks, and at least one synthetic phase-violation attempt is observed blocked — all verified in-session.
- The seed registry file ships containing exactly the three seed gates, and the phase-aware PreToolUse hook is registered in the host repo's hook configuration.
- The State Lifecycle Owner Block is present and every gated skill's phase marker has an owned RETIRE.

## State Lifecycle

| Variable | CREATE | UPDATE | CONSUME | RETIRE |
|----------|--------|--------|---------|--------|
| `<artifacts>/phase-state/<session_id>/<skill>` ({phase, session_id, timestamp}) | the gated skill (brainstorm/sprint/fix-bug) at first phase entry | the gated skill at each phase transition + heartbeat-refresh at each named phase step | the phase-aware PreToolUse hook | the gated skill at skill exit (e.g., sprint Phase I removes it); hook ignores markers past the freshness TTL or with a non-matching session_id; a stale marker is swept at the next start of that skill |
| seed registry file (`registry` path) | af26 sprint ships the 3-gate seed | the brainstorm-confirmed growth step (SC4) appends user-confirmed entries | the PreToolUse hook | never retired — persists as project config |
| override token (`<artifacts>/forbidden-action-override.token`, carrying session_id) | `dso forbidden-action-override` (user-invoked, current-turn-authorized) | consumed (deleted) by the next block | the PreToolUse hook | one-shot: removed on consumption; a token whose session_id differs is never consumed |

## Dependencies

None hard. The reusable override/audit infra (commit-override.sh audit-trail pattern, get_artifacts_dir() resolver, DSO_FBKY_AUTONOMOUS_MODE knob) and the test-gate RED mechanism (record-test-status.sh test-gate-status failed_tests + .test-index RED-zone) already exist in the codebase. relates_to d076-d35e-55db-4843 for the shared session-state-aware hook-installation pattern. (The original stub asserted a hard block on d076; investigation found the reusable infra already shipped independently, so the block is downgraded to relates_to.)

## Out of Scope

- The behavioral-only HARD-GATEs that are not expressible as "block tool X during phase Y" (e.g., "ask one question at a time", "do not speculate root cause") — they remain SKILL.md prose.
- Gates already enforced by existing hooks: no-edit-on-main / no-edit-from-worktree (hook_no_edit_on_main, check-session-merge-only.sh) and no-raw-git-commit (review gate).
- A one-time enumeration of all forbidden-action HARD-GATEs (superseded by seed-and-grow).
- implementation-plan phase-state instrumentation and gates (no seed gate yet; added via SC4 when a concrete gate is confirmed).
- Auto-surfacing of new gates introduced by sprint/fix-bug skill edits made outside a /dso:brainstorm session (growth is brainstorm-scoped).
- Propagation of blocks into CI (the hook is a local tool-use-time gate).
- Cross-platform portability of the exit-2 PreToolUse mechanism to non-POSIX shells (macOS/Linux assumed).

### Tag Integrity Correction (Architecture-vs-Evidence Audit Remediation, 2026-05-16)

Removed two mis-applied tags after surfacing during the 2026-05-16 architecture-vs-evidence audit remediation pass:

- `brainstorm:complete` — REMOVED. The epic description (line 5) explicitly states this is a stub awaiting a dedicated `/dso:brainstorm` session; the Planning Intelligence Log records "stub — scrutiny skipped" for web research, scenario analysis, and LLM-instruction signal. The tag was likely auto-applied when the parent brainstorm named this as a follow-on stub, but no scrutiny pipeline ran against this epic's own SCs.
- `arch-evidence:remediation-needed` — REMOVED. The audit baseline assumed brainstorm-complete deliverables; this epic should not have been included. Once the genuine `/dso:brainstorm` session for this epic runs the full pipeline (including the architecture-vs-evidence probes via the amended brainstorm workflow), the brainstorm-complete tag will be applied legitimately.

### Architectural concerns to feed into the follow-on /dso:brainstorm session

The 2026-05-16 audit flagged probes 1, 3, 4 against this stub's current SCs. The follow-on brainstorm should address:

- **Probe 1 (self-use):** The 2026-05-16 audit asks whether the epic's own sprint must exercise the new PreToolUse hook end-to-end. Add a self-use SC: hook installed + active during the sprint that delivers it; at least one synthetic phase-violation attempt is blocked and one happy-path tool call passes through.
- **Probe 3 (state lifecycle):** Enumerate CREATE / UPDATE / CONSUME / RETIRE owners per (skill, phase) tuple for the durable phase-state metadata the hook reads. The spec currently says only "sourcing phase state from durable session metadata that the relevant skills already track" — that's not a lifecycle table.
- **Probe 4 (bypass governance):** `dso forbidden-action-override --reason="..."` is an explicit bypass. Per the project's architecture-vs-evidence rule, pair with (a) audit-log format and retention, (b) required justification companion rubric, (c) abuse-detection surface at sprint Phase I / end-session closure (count + reasons surfaced before authorizing closure).

### Planning Intelligence Log

- Web research (Step 2): not triggered — sufficient context from in-repo investigation (Explore agent over phase-state sources, sibling override infra, PreToolUse hook contract, the 66 HARD-GATEs) plus a feasibility spike; no external library/API decision.
- Feasibility resolution: triggered and PASSED — a throwaway PreToolUse-hook spike experimentally verified all three seed gates: repo-vs-temp realpath classification + block/allow/fail-open-observable (Gate 1), git status + git worktree enumeration with session-id-encoded branch names (Gate 2), and the test-gate RED-zone reuse (.test-index [first_red_test_name] + test-gate-status failed_tests) for Gate 3.
- Scenario analysis (Step 3): triggered (SCs >= 5); 13 red-team scenarios surfaced. Critical/important folded into the spec: fix-bug RED-signal timing (signal now established by running the RED test at Phase E Step 1, not assumed from commit-time); behavioral-bug exemption requires a positive recorded classification (absence is not a bypass); session-collision (markers session-partitioned by session_id); override self-grant; temp-then-move evasion (Gate 1 also gates Bash move/patch into the repo tree). Moderate residuals (jq/realpath availability, BSD-vs-GNU realpath, cross-platform) recorded as considerations / Out-of-Scope.
- Fidelity review (Step 4): Agent Clarity 3 -> revised (named canonical session_id source, TTL config key, heartbeat trigger, registry/format pointers); Scope 4 (pass; SC6 demoted to Closure Check, SC4 brainstorm-scope documented); Value 3 -> revised (dropped implementation-plan instrumentation per YAGNI, added shadow/log-only baseline mode). One revision cycle (REVISION_CYCLES=1).
- Prompt alignment (Step 5): triggered (LLM-instruction signal — epic modifies agent control surfaces: a blocking PreToolUse hook, a non-self-grantable override, a brainstorm gate-classification step). bot-psychologist returned 6 risks; folded: override must require an explicit current-turn user instruction (not mere interactive presence); growth step uses a neutral fixed template with no nudge-to-decline + declines logged; fail-open distinguishes indeterminate-at-start vs went-stale and rate-limits warnings; block messages carry ordered remediation; behavioral-bug exemption hardened.
- Architectural probe (class:architectural): run — scaffold produced; gate satisfied.
- Cross-epic scan (Step 2.25): focused scan over af26's relates_to set (3c01, 7510, 9778, 99f1, ab57) + sibling-infra epics d076/750c. Both d076 and 750c are CLOSED; investigation found the reusable override/audit + session-state-aware hook-installation infra already shipped independently, so the stub's HARD block on d076 was downgraded to relates_to. No new conflicts surfaced.
- Scale context (Step 0): not applicable — developer-tooling; no record/traffic axis.
- Complexity routing signal: success_criteria_count = 5 (plus State Lifecycle + Closure Checks) — would route to full /dso:preplanning.
- User-directed design decisions: seed-and-grow (3 seed gates); brainstorm-confirmed growth; fail-open + observable; self-use dogfood; keep all 3 gates with Gate 3 reusing the test-gate RED mechanism; Gate 1 repo-only (temp allowed); Gate 2 session-scoped harvest/commit; Option A per-skill session-partitioned phase markers with TTL/heartbeat/owned-RETIRE staleness defenses.
- Provenance note: prior 2026-05-18 tag-integrity correction removed a mis-applied brainstorm:complete (stub). This pass ran the full canonical scrutiny pipeline, so the tag is now legitimately applied. Bug 01b9-3359-7df3-45cf filed for the non-idempotent migration that resurrected the stale tag.
